title: One bank, one family, one loan
subtitle: What today’s risks would do, as what-ifs
note: The bank and its figures are made up. The family is Antevo’s example household with a made-up loan. The risks, the falls and the loan’s position are the Antevo tools’ answers on the date shown. A what-if is not a forecast.

tries.label: The same morning, from four seats
tries.source: Antevo Wealth, Executive Brief, Tremor Watch and Strategy Radar, 26 Nov 2026. Each risk is tied to one named what-if from a fixed list that Antevo keeps. A what-if is not a forecast: the risk may play out differently, or not at all. The bank, its figures and its assumptions are made up and typed in by the bank. Antevo supplies the risks and the falls; the rest is arithmetic.

items.name: The chief executive · what is unfolding
evidence: Rising: AI borrowers find the debt market shut (54 mornings on the list); fourteen partners answer the tariff proposals (23); strikes reach Saudi oil facilities (17)
Stable: the bond shelter fails (38); leveraged funds are forced to cut together (11)
Markets in the week of 20 Nov: Elevated, 2.4 times a normal week (3.8 the week before)

items.name: The bank’s own plan · if leveraged funds cut together
evidence: Antevo’s what-if (shares down a fifth everywhere): cautious −15.4%, balanced −20.0%, growth −25.9%
The bank’s own split of client assets: 30% cautious, 45% balanced, 25% growth, so client assets fall 20.1%
The bank’s own income: 62% fees on assets (−20.1%), 14% dealing (+5%, its assumption), 24% interest (−8%, its assumption)

items.name: The client banker · one family, one loan
evidence: CHF 4.5m borrowed against a growth portfolio worth CHF 9.70m: 46.4%
Agreed limit 55%; the level where the bank may ask for more security 65%
The portfolio can fall 15.7% before the limit and 28.7% before the second level
Under the broad sell-off what-if it falls 25.9%: the loan stands at 62.6%
Back to the limit in that what-if: CHF 544,768 repaid, or CHF 990,487 more pledged

items.name: The business client · a clothing importer
items.verdict: Two of eight lines touch it
evidence: Tariffs formally proposed on fourteen partners, possibly from January: act when final lists and rates are published, or a partner announces countermeasures
Bangladesh’s garment workers won a minimum wage rise of more than a third: act when suppliers quote higher spring prices or tariff lists confirm duties on clothing

items.do: Start with the cost, not the headline
items.why: As a what-if the tariffs take 3.9% off this bank’s client assets; a broad fall in shares, 20.1%.

items.do: Keep your own assumptions apart from the answers
items.why: The falls are Antevo’s. The split and the two assumptions are the bank’s.

items.do: Go to the meeting with the loan’s own numbers
items.why: CHF 0.54m repaid or CHF 0.99m more pledged would bring it back to the limit in that what-if.

items.do: See what the client holds elsewhere
items.why: The bank sees CHF 29.6m of the family’s CHF 35.6m.

items.do: Ask the business client one question
items.why: Whether its products are on the final tariff lists, and what its spring quotes say.

sections.title: The loan against every what-if
sections.so_what: Today’s list is what is in the news. The full list shows how much room the loan really has.
evidence: 35 what-ifs run on the pledged portfolio
10 take the loan past the agreed limit
4 take it past the level where the bank may ask for more security
The furthest: a replay of the crash of 2000 to 2002
sections.source: Antevo Wealth, 26 Nov 2026. What a bank does when a loan passes a level is set by the loan agreement. Nothing here says a margin call will happen.

sections.title: Four risks, one loan
sections.so_what: One risk on today’s list takes this loan past its limit. The banker can name it.
evidence: Shares down a fifth everywhere: 63%
Trade war: 52%
Money leaves technology shares: 51%
Interest rates two points higher: 46%, unchanged

sections.title: The bank’s client assets, risk by risk
sections.so_what: The same split of client assets, four what-ifs, four very different mornings.
evidence: Leveraged funds cut together: −20.1%
AI borrowers find the debt market shut: −4.0%
Partners answer the tariffs: −3.9%
The bond shelter fails: −0.6%
Strikes on Saudi oil sites: no what-if fits, so no figure
sections.source: Falls: Antevo Wealth, 26 Nov 2026. Split: the bank’s own.

sections.title: What the bank does not see
sections.so_what: The client’s funds elsewhere hold the same technology companies as the pledged portfolio.
evidence: At this bank: CHF 29.6m
At two other banks: CHF 6.0m, in three funds
Net worth after the loan: CHF 31.1m

links.text: The tariffs lead the news and take 3.9% off the bank’s client assets. A broad fall in shares, a quieter line on the list, takes 20.1%.
The same what-if that takes 14% off the bank’s income takes the client’s loan past its limit. One morning, both sides of the balance sheet.
